name: Koh Samui & Koh Phangan
tagline: Thailand's Gulf coast islands, Koh Samui's palm-lined resort beaches paired with Koh Phangan's Full Moon Party energy and its own quieter corners.
highlight: Sunset over the Big Buddha at Wat Phra Yai, its golden statue catching the last light above Koh Samui's northeastern coast.
shortDescription: The Gulf of Thailand's two most popular islands, Koh Samui's resort beaches paired with Koh Phangan's nightlife and quieter yoga retreats.
metaDescription: A Koh Samui and Koh Phangan travel guide: the best beaches, the Full Moon Party, when to go and a practical four-day itinerary.
knownFor: Resort beaches, the Full Moon Party, Ang Thong Marine Park
goodFor: Beaches, nightlife, a Gulf coast alternative to Phuket

image.alt: Chaweng Beach's palm-lined sand on Koh Samui

intro: Koh Samui and Koh Phangan sit on Thailand's Gulf coast, reachable directly from Bangkok without the transfer through Phuket or Krabi that the Andaman coast requires, and together offer a different island rhythm from the country's west side.

Koh Samui, the larger and more developed of the two, pairs palm-lined resort beaches like Chaweng and Lamai with an increasingly serious dining scene and family-friendly infrastructure, while Koh Phangan, a short ferry away, is best known internationally for its monthly Full Moon Party but holds a quieter side too, from yoga retreats to secluded northern coves.

The islands' position on the Gulf side also means their rainy season runs on different timing from the Andaman coast, keeping Koh Samui comparatively dry even when Phuket and Krabi are seeing their heaviest rains — a useful fact for planning around Thailand's seasons.

whyVisit.intro: Koh Samui and Koh Phangan's case is a different island rhythm from Phuket and Krabi, reachable directly from Bangkok without an Andaman coast transfer.

points.title: Koh Samui's beaches are excellent
points.text: Chaweng and Lamai offer long, palm-lined sand with a well-developed range of hotels and restaurants behind them.

points.title: Koh Phangan delivers a singular nightlife experience
points.text: The Full Moon Party is unlike anything else in Thailand, drawing visitors specifically for that one night each lunar month.

points.title: Both islands also have a quieter side
points.text: Koh Phangan's north coast and Koh Samui's smaller bays offer real escape from the main resort strips.

points.title: The Gulf coast's rainy season runs differently
points.text: Useful for planning a trip around the Andaman coast's wetter months from May to October.

points.title: Ang Thong Marine Park is a spectacular day trip
points.text: A cluster of limestone islands and hidden lagoons reachable by boat from either island.

attractionsIntro: The islands' essential sights, spanning Koh Samui's beaches and temples and Koh Phangan's coastline and party scene.

attractions.name: Chaweng Beach

image.alt: Chaweng Beach's palm-lined sand on Koh Samui

attractions.text: Koh Samui's longest and most developed beach, its palm-lined sand backed by a wide range of resorts, restaurants and bars.
attractions.tip: The northern end of Chaweng is noticeably quieter than the busy central strip, while staying within easy walking distance of it.

attractions.name: Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai)
attractions.text: A 12-metre golden Buddha statue on a small island connected to Koh Samui by causeway, one of the island's most recognisable landmarks.
attractions.tip: Visit for sunset, when the statue and surrounding temple are lit gold by the setting sun.

attractions.name: Ang Thong National Marine Park
attractions.text: A stunning archipelago of forty-two limestone islands, hidden lagoons and emerald water, reachable by day-trip boat from either Koh Samui or Koh Phangan.
attractions.tip: The full-day tour rewards the extra time over a half-day version — there's considerably more to see across the park's islands.

attractions.name: Haad Rin Beach, Koh Phangan
attractions.text: The site of the monthly Full Moon Party, transforming from a quiet beach by day into one of Southeast Asia's most famous all-night parties.
attractions.tip: Check the current Full Moon Party schedule ahead — dates shift slightly around the actual lunar full moon and local calendar adjustments.

attractions.name: Bottle Beach (Haad Khuad), Koh Phangan
attractions.text: A secluded northern-coast beach reachable only by boat or a challenging jungle trek, offering a considerably quieter alternative to Haad Rin.
attractions.tip: Take the boat rather than the jungle trek unless you're an experienced, well-prepared hiker — the trail is difficult.

attractions.name: The Hin Ta and Hin Yai rock formations
attractions.text: Naturally formed rock shapes on Koh Samui's Lamai coast that have earned a cheeky local nickname for their resemblance to certain body parts, a popular quick photo stop.
attractions.tip: A short, easy stop worth combining with a Lamai Beach visit rather than a dedicated trip on its own.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the beaches, the islands reward boat trips, wellness retreats and, on Koh Phangan, a famous night out.

thingsToDo.title: Attend the Full Moon Party
thingsToDo.text: Koh Phangan's monthly beach party at Haad Rin draws thousands for all-night dancing, fire shows and a unique atmosphere found nowhere else in Thailand.
thingsToDo.tip: Book accommodation well ahead if visiting specifically for the party — rooms on Koh Phangan fill up fast around the date.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat trip to Ang Thong Marine Park
thingsToDo.text: A full-day boat tour through the marine park's limestone islands, including a climb to a viewpoint overlooking a hidden emerald lagoon.
thingsToDo.tip: The viewpoint climb is steep — comfortable shoes make a real difference on this trip.

thingsToDo.title: Try a yoga or wellness retreat on Koh Phangan
thingsToDo.text: Koh Phangan has developed a serious wellness and yoga retreat scene, particularly around the island's quieter west and north coasts.
thingsToDo.tip: Book well ahead for a dedicated retreat centre, several of which run structured multi-day or weeklong programmes.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Koh Samui's Fisherman's Village
thingsToDo.text: Bophut's old fishing village neighbourhood offers a more relaxed evening scene than Chaweng, with a weekly Friday night walking street market.
thingsToDo.tip: Time a visit for Friday evening, when the walking street market is at its liveliest.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel or dive around Koh Tao
thingsToDo.text: A third nearby island, one of Thailand's best and cheapest places to learn to dive, reachable by ferry from either Koh Samui or Koh Phangan.
thingsToDo.tip: A day trip covers snorkelling well, but a multi-day stay is worth it if you want to get certified to dive.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a waterfall on Koh Samui
thingsToDo.text: Na Muang and Hin Lad waterfalls offer a refreshing inland break from the beaches, both an easy day trip from the main resort areas.
thingsToDo.tip: Visit after rain for the fullest flow, though the falls run year-round even in the dry season.

foodIntro: Both islands offer standard Thai cuisine alongside a strong seafood tradition and, on Koh Phangan, health-focused café culture.

foods.name: Fresh grilled seafood
foods.text: Prawns, squid and whole fish grilled simply and priced by weight, excellent around both islands' beachfront restaurants.
foods.whereToTry: Beachfront restaurants on Chaweng and Bophut, and around Haad Rin on Koh Phangan.

foods.name: Pad thai

image.alt: A plate of pad thai with pork

foods.text: Available across both islands as elsewhere in Thailand, good from street stalls and beachfront vendors.
foods.whereToTry: Street stalls throughout Chaweng, Lamai and Haad Rin.

foods.name: Som tam (green papaya salad)

image.file: File:Som Tam green papaya salad, Bangkok, Thailand.jpg
image.alt: Som tam, spicy green papaya salad, with fresh chillies and beans

foods.text: A fiery, refreshing salad widely available across both islands, a good counterpoint to a rich seafood meal.
foods.whereToTry: Local Thai restaurants and street stalls on both islands.

foods.name: Healthy café fare on Koh Phangan
foods.text: Koh Phangan's wellness and yoga scene has fuelled a strong café culture of smoothie bowls, fresh juices and vegetarian food.
foods.whereToTry: Cafés around Srithanu and the island's west coast, the heart of its wellness scene.

foods.name: Fresh tropical fruit
foods.text: Mango, dragon fruit, rambutan and mangosteen, at their best sold fresh from roadside stalls and markets on both islands.
foods.whereToTry: Markets and roadside stalls throughout Koh Samui and Koh Phangan.

accommodation.intro: Koh Samui and Koh Phangan each offer distinct areas depending on whether beaches, nightlife or wellness matter most.

areas.name: Chaweng, Koh Samui
areas.bestFor: The widest range of hotels, restaurants and nightlife
areas.text: Koh Samui's busiest beach strip, with good infrastructure for a first-time visit to the island.

areas.name: Bophut (Fisherman's Village), Koh Samui
areas.bestFor: A quieter, more relaxed evening atmosphere
areas.text: A charming old fishing village neighbourhood with boutique hotels and a weekly walking street market.

areas.name: Haad Rin, Koh Phangan
areas.bestFor: The Full Moon Party and beach nightlife
areas.text: The island's main party hub, central for Full Moon Party access though considerably livelier than Koh Phangan's other coasts.

areas.name: Srithanu, Koh Phangan
areas.bestFor: Yoga retreats and a wellness-focused atmosphere
areas.text: The island's quieter west-coast wellness hub, a different side of Koh Phangan from Haad Rin's party scene.

gettingThere.intro: Koh Samui has its own airport with direct flights from Bangkok, while Koh Phangan is reached onward by ferry.

options.text: Direct flights from [[bangkok|Bangkok]], landing at a distinctive open-air airport built and run by Bangkok Airways.
options.detail: A taxi or pre-booked transfer covers the journey to Chaweng or Bophut.

options.mode: Ferry between Koh Samui and Koh Phangan
options.text: Frequent daily ferries connect the two islands in about 30–45 minutes.
options.detail: Several ferry operators run the route — a through-ticket from the mainland often includes this leg.

options.text: A more budget-friendly route via an overnight train or bus from [[bangkok|Bangkok]] to Surat Thani, then a ferry onward.
options.detail: Combination train-and-ferry tickets are convenient and widely sold by travel agents in Bangkok.

gettingAround.intro: Both islands rely on songthaews, taxis and rented scooters, since neither has extensive public transport.

options.text: Circle Koh Samui's ring road and Koh Phangan's main routes, a cheap way to get between beaches.
options.detail: Confirm the fare before boarding, as prices can vary between drivers.

options.text: A popular way to explore both islands independently, particularly Koh Phangan's quieter, more spread-out coastline.
options.detail: An International Driving Permit and a proper helmet are important — insurance often excludes claims without one.

options.text: Widely available on Koh Samui, less consistently on Koh Phangan, where negotiation is more common.
options.detail: Agree the fare before setting off if no meter or app pricing is available.

bestTime.headline: December–April, for the Gulf coast's driest season
bestTime.summary: Koh Samui and Koh Phangan run on a different rainy-season timing from Thailand's Andaman coast, staying comparatively dry even when Phuket sees heavier rain.

seasons.text: The most reliable weather for beaches and boat trips, alongside the busiest crowds and highest prices.
Still largely dry, hot, with thinner crowds than the December–January peak.
The Gulf coast's own rainy stretch, typically shorter and less severe than the Andaman coast's monsoon, but worth checking forecasts around.

bestTime.avoid: Late October to early December for the wettest stretch of the Gulf coast's own shorter monsoon period, which runs opposite to the Andaman coast's timing.

itinerary.title: Four days on Koh Samui and Koh Phangan
itinerary.intro: Koh Samui's beaches and sights first, then a ferry across to Koh Phangan for a different island atmosphere.

days.title: Arrive on Koh Samui
days.morning: Arrive and settle into Chaweng or Bophut.
days.afternoon: A first swim at Chaweng Beach.

days.title: Ang Thong Marine Park
days.morning: A full-day boat tour into the marine park.
days.afternoon: The viewpoint climb over the hidden lagoon.
days.evening: A relaxed dinner back on Koh Samui.

days.title: Ferry to Koh Phangan
days.afternoon: Explore Haad Rin or the quieter Srithanu coast.
days.evening: The Full Moon Party, if your dates align, or a quieter beach dinner.

days.title: Koh Phangan's quieter side
days.morning: A boat trip to Bottle Beach in the north.
days.afternoon: Free time or a yoga class in Srithanu.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on booking, timing and transport that make a real difference to a Koh Samui and Koh Phangan trip.
tips: Book accommodation on Koh Phangan well ahead if timing your visit around the Full Moon Party — rooms fill up fast.
Check the current Full Moon Party date ahead, since it shifts slightly around the actual lunar cycle and local adjustments.
Wear a proper helmet if renting a scooter, and check your travel insurance covers it.
Book the full-day rather than half-day Ang Thong Marine Park tour if you have the time — it covers considerably more.
Consider the mainland train-and-ferry route via Surat Thani for a more budget-friendly journey than flying.
Pack for both beach days and a night out — the islands' dress codes are casual but the Full Moon Party gets messy.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Koh Samui and Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Four to five. Three covers Koh Samui's beaches with a day trip; five allows a proper ferry crossing to Koh Phangan and its quieter northern coast without feeling rushed.

faq.q: Do I have to attend the Full Moon Party?
faq.a: No — Koh Phangan has a quieter side too, from yoga retreats around Srithanu to secluded beaches like Bottle Beach, well suited to visitors who'd rather skip the party scene entirely.

faq.q: Is Koh Samui or Phuket better for a first trip?
faq.a: Koh Samui offers a quieter, more relaxed resort atmosphere and easier direct flights from Bangkok; Phuket offers more nightlife and a wider range of nearby islands to explore. Both work well as a first Thailand beach trip.

faq.q: How do I get between Koh Samui and Koh Phangan?
faq.a: By ferry — frequent daily crossings run between the two islands in about 30–45 minutes, and combination tickets from the mainland often include this leg automatically.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: December to April offers the Gulf coast's driest, most reliable weather. Late October to early December brings the region's own shorter rainy stretch, worth checking forecasts around if your dates are flexible.
